member.summary:
Growing-degree-day harvest predictor with an analog-year ensemble for the part of the season that has not happened yet.
The season is split into three segments: 1. planting -> yesterday reanalysis (what actually happened) 2. today -> today + 16 days numerical weather forecast 3. beyond replay of the last N years' real temperatures
Segment 3 is the interesting one. Rather than inventing a symmetric error bar, we re-run the remaining thermal requirement against each of the last N years' actual weather. That yields N plausible harvest dates; the 10th/50th/90th percentiles become the earliest / expected / latest window. The spread is then a real statement about how variable this location's climate is, not a guess.
